spans.s:
न 1. न, the twentieth consonant of the
alphabet, and the fifth letter of the fourth or dental
class, having much the sound of the English n in
tenth.
—न-कार, अस्, m. the letter or sound न.

न 2. न, ind. a particle of negation equi-
valent to ‘not,’ ‘no,’ ‘nor,’ ‘neither’ [cf. नो, न-
नु, न-हि, न-तराम्], and in the Veda a particle of
comparison; it is used as a negative particle in wishing,
requesting, and commanding (e. g. न मा गरन्
नद्यः, let not the waters swallow me; नावमन्-
येत कञ्चन, let him not despise any one), but not
in prohibition before an imperative, and not before
the aorist when it has lost its augment and stands for
an imperative (in both which cases मा, q. v., is used).
When joined with the potential, न may often have
the sense of ‘that not,’ ‘lest,’ ‘for fear lest’ (e. g.
न त्वां शपेत्, lest he should curse thee). In
argumentative writings न often comes at the end of
a hypothetical argument in the sense ‘not so’ (e. g.
ननु न किञ्चिन् मानम्

न, now if it be
said that there is no proof, not so). Two नस् are
not unfrequently used in the same sentence to intensify
an affirmation (e. g. न खलु न तत् करिष्यामि,
I will most certainly do that; न तु जातु न, most
assuredly), or any other negative particle may be
joined with न with the same effect (e. g. नादण्ड्यो
ऽस्ति, he is not to go unpunished, i. e. he must cer-
tainly be punished). When a negation has to be
repeated in successive clauses of a sentence or in
successive sentences, न may be simply repeated or
may be strengthened by one of the particles उत, च,
अपि, चापि, वा, अथवा (e. g. नाहम् अस्यारण्यस्य
देवता न चाप्य् अस्य गिरेः, I am not the deity of
this forest nor of this mountain), or the negative is
not expressed in the second clause but represented
by वा or अपि वा or च standing alone (e. g. न हृष्-
यति ग्लायति वा, he neither rejoices nor desponds),
or two clauses may have the negative particle and
not a third (e. g. न देवेषु न यक्षेषु मानु-
षेष्व् अपि चान्येषु तादृग् रूपवती दृष्ट-
पूर्वा, neither among gods nor Yakṣas nor other
mortals has so beautiful a female been before seen).
न is sometimes placed before round or collective
numbers to denote a deficiency, the deficient number
being prefixed in the inst. or abl. case (e. g. एकया
or एकेन न विंशतिः, not twenty by one, i. e. nine-
teen; पञ्चभिर् न चत्वारि शतानि, 395). When
न is the negative of the simple idea expressed by a
word, it may be regarded as compounded with it,
and is then identical with 3. अ, q. v. (e. g. न-विद्वस्,
unwise; नाधीत, unread; न-किञ्चन, q. v.) न
is often joined with other particles, e. g. न च, न
चापि, नापि, नोत, न वा, नैव, न चैव, नापि
च, न तु, न त्वेव, न त्वेव तु, न चेत् (see
चेद्), न खलु, न ह (after this last a verb is
said to retain its accent if used in the future with an
imperative sense, Pāṇ.

). न is frequently
used in early Vedic composition as a particle of com-
parison = ‘like,’ ‘as,’ ‘as it were’ (e. g. त्वा नावं
न धीमहि, we meditate on thee like a boat; cf.
3. अ, which also in a few instances = ‘like’); it is also
found in this sense in the later artificial poems; [cf.
Lat. ne, non; Gr. νη in νη-κηδής;
Lith. ne; Slav. ne; Goth. ni, ne, nei; Angl. Sax.
na; Old Germ. ni; Hib. ni.]

न 3. न, अस्, m. a N. of Buddha; binding,
tying, a band; one who is praised; a N. of Gaṇeśa
(= द्वि-रण्ड?); a jewel, pearl; war; giving, a
gift; welfare, prosperity; (आ), f. the navel; a musical
instrument; knowledge; (अस्, आ, अम्), thin, spare;
vacant, empty; identical, same, like; unvexed, un-
wearied; undivided, unbroken.

न 4. न, (in prosody) a tribrach or foot
of three short syllables.
ना ना, ind. = न, no, not.
